input:
In fd, include hidden entries but keep ignore rules. Which flag?
A. --hidden
B. --no-ignore
C. --type directory

In fd, disable ignore-file filtering without enabling hidden entries. Which flag?
A. --follow
B. --no-ignore
C. --hidden

With fd, select only files with extension parquet. Which command?
A. fd -t parquet
B. fd --size parquet
C. fd -e parquet

With fd, return only directories matching cache. Which command?
A. fd -t d cache
B. fd -t f cache
C. fd -e cache

With fd, cap recursive traversal at depth two. Which flag?
A. --threads 2
B. --max-depth 2
C. --size 2

In fd, treat the pattern as a shell glob. Which flag?
A. --fixed-strings
B. --full-path
C. --glob

In fd, force case-sensitive pattern matching. Which flag?
A. --case-sensitive
B. --ignore-case
C. --hidden

In fd, match the full path instead of only the filename. Which flag?
A. --list-details
B. --full-path
C. --absolute-path

In fd, follow directory symlinks while searching. Which flag?
A. --hidden
B. --no-ignore
C. --follow

In fd, exclude paths matching a glob vendor. Which flag?
A. --exclude vendor
B. --extension vendor
C. --type vendor

Using Mike Farah yq v4, read replicas under spec. Which expression?
A. del(.spec.replicas)
B. .spec.replicas
C. .spec | keys

Using Mike Farah yq v4, write a change back to the input file. Which flag?
A. -n
B. -o=json
C. -i

Using Mike Farah yq v4, assign integer 4 to replicas under spec. Which expression?
A. .spec.replicas = 4
B. .spec.replicas == 4
C. .spec.replicas | length

Using Mike Farah yq v4, remove the debug key. Which expression?
A. keys
B. del(.debug)
C. .debug = true

Using Mike Farah yq v4, select the first element of items. Which expression?
A. .items[1]
B. .items | length
C. .items[0]

Using Mike Farah yq v4, count elements of items. Which expression?
A. .items | length
B. .items[]
C. .items | keys

Using Mike Farah yq v4, retain only objects with enabled equal to true. Which expression?
A. .[] | .enabled = false
B. .[] | select(.enabled == true)
C. .[] | del(.enabled)

Using Mike Farah yq v4, read environment variable PORT as a string. Which expression?
A. env(PORT)
B. .PORT
C. strenv(PORT)

Using Mike Farah yq v4, emit JSON rather than YAML. Which flag?
A. -o=json
B. -i
C. -n

Using Mike Farah yq v4, append api to an existing services array. Which expression?
A. del(.services)
B. .services += ["api"]
C. .services = "api"

For lsblk, choose JSON output. Which flag?
A. --pairs
B. --raw
C. --json

For lsblk, report sizes as bytes. Which flag?
A. --bytes
B. --fs
C. --ascii

For lsblk, select exactly NAME and SIZE columns. Which flag?
A. --exclude 8
B. --output NAME,SIZE
C. --sort NAME

For lsblk, suppress the header row. Which flag?
A. --nodeps
B. --list
C. --noheadings

For lsblk, request a flat list rather than a tree. Which flag?
A. --list
B. --tree
C. --inverse

For lsblk, show full device paths. Which flag?
A. --perms
B. --paths
C. --pairs

For lsblk, show filesystem-related information. Which flag?
A. --discard
B. --topology
C. --fs

For lsblk /dev/sda, suppress child and holder devices. Which flag?
A. --nodeps
B. --noheadings
C. --all

For lsblk, output key=value pairs. Which flag?
A. --bytes
B. --pairs
C. --json

For lsblk, sort the output by SIZE. Which flag?
A. --output SIZE
B. --exclude SIZE
C. --sort SIZE

Using ethtool, display ring parameters for eno1. Which command?
A. ethtool -g eno1

Using ethtool, display interrupt-coalescing settings for eno1. Which command?
A. ethtool -l eno1

Using ethtool, display pause-frame settings for eno1. Which command?
A. ethtool -i eno1

Using ethtool, display channel counts for eno1. Which command?
A. ethtool -l eno1

In Neovim normal mode, move to the first line. Which command?
A. $
B. gg
C. G

In Neovim normal mode, move to the last line. Which command?
A. gg
B. 0
C. G

In Neovim normal mode, move to the end of the current line. Which command?
A. $
B. 0
C. gg

In Neovim normal mode, delete the current line. Which command?
A. p
B. dd
C. yy

In Neovim normal mode, copy the current line. Which command?
A. dd
B. u
C. yy

In Neovim normal mode, undo the most recent change. Which command?
A. u
B. p
C. dd

In Neovim normal mode, redo an undone change. Which key?
A. CTRL-B
B. CTRL-R
C. CTRL-F

In Neovim normal mode, paste after the cursor. Which command?
A. P
B. yy
C. p

In Neovim, save the current file without quitting. Which Ex command?
A. :w
B. :q!
C. :e!

In Neovim, quit the current window discarding unsaved changes. Which Ex command?
A. :wq
B. :q!
C. :w
